title: Tokenization pipeline: prefetch cache & short‑circuit fast path
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Reduce prefill-side CPU and latency overhead by adding a light-weight prefetch cache for common prompt prefixes and a deterministic short-circuit path for already-tokenized headers. Integrate hints into the kernel selector so decode scheduling can assume lower prefill overhead for cached prefixes.
motivation: Observed prefill-side overhead dominating end-to-end latency for low-token decode requests (chat turn sizes <= 32 tokens). Platform telemetry shows 40–60% of CPU time per request spent in tokenization and prefix handling during bursts. Reducing this improves p50/p95 latency and lowers per-token cost on shared dedicated nodes.
background: Related experiments exist in other tickets but are focused on tokenizer microbatching or generic prefill caches. This work differs by: 1) focusing a tiny LRU prefetch specifically for static/common prefixes (system prompts, standard headers), 2) short‑circuit path that bypasses the full tokenization pipeline for pretokenized items, and 3) surfaced affinity hints to kernel selection and decode scheduler to enable more aggressive batching when prefill is cheap.
proposal:
- Implement a per-tenant LRU prefetch cache storing a compact pretokenized representation (byte-offsets + token-ids) for up to 128 hot prefixes. Keep entries memory-light (~200–800 bytes each).
- Add a deterministic fast-path that detects 'pretokenized header' markers on incoming requests and performs a zero-copy stitch into the decode KV cache, skipping regex and normalization passes.
- Emit an "affinity_hint": {"prefill_cost":"low" | "normal"} from tokenization stage into the request metadata so the kernel scheduler can prefer larger microbatches or switch to higher-efficiency kernels for decode.
- Add adaptive eviction TTL: entries observed being used >3x in last 5 minutes gain extended TTL; rarely used entries expire faster.
implementation_plan: Design compact pretokenized wire format (token ids + byte spans + checksum) - RFC in docs
Backend: implement per-tenant LRU store in serving runtime (C++), with metrics and debug endpoint
Fast-path: add marker parsing in request preprocessor; implement zero-copy KV stitching into runtime cache
Kernel hint: extend request proto to include prefill_cost hint; update kernel selector heuristics to account for low prefill cost
E2E tests: correctness suite for edge cases (unicode normalization, fallback to full tokenization), performance harness for tokens/sec and CPU profiles
Rollout: canary on 10% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants; feature gated by config flag
acceptance_criteria: p50 prefill latency for 8-token system-prefix requests improves by >= 2x on test cluster
end-to-end p95 latency for small-turn (<=32 token) requests reduced by >= 10% on average
no accuracy regressions in canonical eval prompts (tokenization must be byte-for-byte consistent) - pass regression suite
resource overhead per serving process < 12 MB for full cache (128 entries) and scales predictably
feature flag controls and rollout steps documented; canary rollout executed with monitoring dashboards
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Spike implemented a prototype LRU prefetch in Python harness. Microbench shows 2.3x median prefill speedup for synthetic hot-prefix workload (8–12 token prefixes).
2026-03-06: C++ runtime interface proposed. RFC posted: /docs/rfcs/token-prefetch-rfc.md (see linked_docs).

2026-03-09: Discovered edge-case: some 'system' prefixes include unprintable control chars that current pretokenizer normalizes differently than legacy pipeline. Added unit tests and will add checksum validation to pretokenized entries.

2026-03-12: Kernel selector change drafted. Simple heuristic: if prefill_cost==low, prefer larger microbatches (up to +30% batch size) and enable fused-attention kernel for short sequences. Need perf regressions validation.
2026-03-14: Integration smoke tests pass on staging; memory overhead measured ~9MB per process with 128-entry cache. Preparing canary config and dashboards.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Memory vs latency: cache consumes per-process memory and increases working set; must cap entries and offer tenant-level limits
Stale/invalid prefixes: if tenant updates a system prompt, pretokenized cache may serve stale tokens until invalidation — require checksum on request and explicit invalidation API
Security: cached tokens are derived from customer data; must encrypt cache in Private deployments and document KMS requirements (security_review_required=true)
Complexity: adding affinity hints to kernel selection couples tokenizer changes with kernel heuristics; increases coordination surface between runtime and kernel teams
notes_from_reviews: Liam: advised to avoid enabling fused-attention kernel for variable-length microbatches without ensuring KV-layout compatibility. Suggest a gating test.
Priya: requested encryption-at-rest for Private deployment caches and explicit opt-out for telemetry. Marked security_review_required=true.
Sofia: requested an observability plan: counters for cache hits/misses, hit-latency, and a histogram of prefill_cost distribution
observability_plan: Expose metrics: token_prefetch_hits, token_prefetch_misses, prefill_cost_histogram, prefill_latency_ms; add a per-tenant dashboard and an alert for >10% cache eviction rate over 5m
rollout_plan: Feature flag default OFF. Canary 5% -> 10% -> 50% over two weeks with automated rollback if p95 latency increases or error rate rises >0.5%.
